title: LINQ to SQL, and projections
summary: Why some LINQ becomes SQL, and why selecting only what you need beats loading entities.

steps.title: Expression trees
body: `db.Books.Where(b => b.Year > 1950)` looks like LINQ over a list, but it is not. `db.Books` is an `IQueryable<Book>`, and on an `IQueryable` the lambda is not compiled into code: it is captured as an **expression tree**, a data structure that describes `b.Year > 1950`.
When you finally run the query, EF Core walks that tree and **translates** it into SQL for the provider. That is why:
- the work happens in the database (filtering a million rows there, not in your process),
- you can only use things EF Core knows how to translate: properties, operators, many `string` and `Math` methods, `Contains` on a list... but not your own methods,
- a mistake can compile fine and fail only when the query runs.
The same lambda on a `List<Book>` is ordinary compiled code. **Where the query starts decides where it runs.**

steps.prompt: What is `db.Books.Where(b => b.Pages > 300)` before you enumerate it?
options: A description of a query (an expression tree) that has not run yet
A list of the books with more than 300 pages
A compiled delegate that EF Core calls for each row
steps.explain: It is an `IQueryable<Book>` holding an expression tree. Nothing ran. `ToList()`, `First()`, `Count()` or a `foreach` will translate it to SQL and run it.

steps.title: Projections
body: Loading entities reads **every column** and **tracks** every object, ready for `SaveChanges`. For a screen that shows titles and author names, that is wasted work. Say what you need with `Select`:
```csharp
var rows = db.Books
.Where(b => b.Year > 1950)
.Select(b => new { b.Title, Author = b.Author.Name })
.ToList();
```text
SELECT "b"."Title", "a"."Name" AS "Author"
FROM "Books" AS "b"
INNER JOIN "Authors" AS "a" ON "b"."AuthorId" = "a"."Id"
WHERE "b"."Year" > 1950
Three wins:
- **Fewer columns** cross the wire: two, not every column of two tables.
- **No `Include` needed**: navigating to `b.Author.Name` inside `Select` makes EF Core write the join.
- **No tracking**: the results are not entities, so the context keeps no snapshots of them.
Project into an anonymous type, a record (`new BookRow(b.Title, b.Author.Name)`), or a single value (`Select(b => b.Title)`).

code: var query = db.Books.Select(b => new { b.Title, Author = b.Author.Name });
public Author Author { get; set; } = null!;
protected override void OnConfiguring(DbContextOptionsBuilder options) => options.UseSqlite("Data Source=library.db");
steps.explain: Only the projected columns are selected, so `Pages` never leaves the database. Reaching for `b.Author.Name` makes EF Core join `Authors` for you.

code: var leGuin = new Author { Name = "Le Guin", Country = "US" };
var herbert = new Author { Name = "Herbert", Country = "US" };
var austen = new Author { Name = "Austen", Country = "UK" };
new Book { Title = "Earthsea", Year = 1968, Pages = 183, Genre = "Fantasy", Author = leGuin },
new Book { Title = "The Dispossessed", Year = 1974, Pages = 387, Genre = "SciFi", Author = leGuin },
new Book { Title = "Dune", Year = 1965, Pages = 412, Genre = "SciFi", Author = herbert },
new Book { Title = "Emma", Year = 1815, Pages = 474, Genre = "Classic", Author = austen },
new Book { Title = "Persuasion", Year = 1817, Pages = 249, Genre = "Classic", Author = austen });
var rows = db.Books.Select(b => new { b.Title, b.Author.Name }).ToList();
public Author Author { get; set; } = null!;
protected override void OnConfiguring(DbContextOptionsBuilder options) => options.UseSqlite("Data Source=library.db");
steps.explain: Loading entities tracks every one of them: five books and three authors. A projection returns plain values the context does not track at all.

steps.prompt: Project each author into a summary: the name and how many books they wrote.
steps.explain: `Select` builds the record, `a.Books.Count()` becomes a `COUNT(*)` subquery, and `ToList` runs it. No `Include`: the books themselves are never loaded.

items: Change a book's title and save
Delete the books of an author you just loaded
Show a list of titles and author names
Return JSON for a search results page
Count books per genre for a chart
steps.explain: Load (tracked) entities when you will change them. For anything read-only, project the fields you need: less data, no tracking cost, and the shape you want.

steps.title: A catalogue page
prompt: The tests give you this model:
class Author { int Id; string Name; string Country; List<Book> Books; }
class Book   { int Id; string Title; int Year; int Pages; string Genre; int AuthorId; Author Author; }

The tests fill it with five books: Earthsea (Le Guin, 1968, 183 pages, Fantasy), The Dispossessed (Le Guin, 1974, 387, SciFi), Dune (Herbert, 1965, 412, SciFi), Emma (Austen, 1815, 474, Classic) and Persuasion (Austen, 1817, 249, Classic). Le Guin and Herbert are from the US, Austen from the UK.
Write `List<CatalogueRow> Catalogue(LibraryDb db, int minPages)` returning books with at least `minPages` pages, ordered by `Title`, **projected** into
record CatalogueRow(string Title, string Author, int Year);
Declare the record yourself (at the bottom). Do not use `Include` and do not load entities: the tests check that the SQL selects only those three columns.
starter: record CatalogueRow(string Title, string Author, int Year);
solution: record CatalogueRow(string Title, string Author, int Year);
template: var leGuin = new Author { Name = "Le Guin", Country = "US" };
var herbert = new Author { Name = "Herbert", Country = "US" };
var austen = new Author { Name = "Austen", Country = "UK" };
new Book { Title = "Earthsea", Year = 1968, Pages = 183, Genre = "Fantasy", Author = leGuin },
new Book { Title = "The Dispossessed", Year = 1974, Pages = 387, Genre = "SciFi", Author = leGuin },
new Book { Title = "Dune", Year = 1965, Pages = 412, Genre = "SciFi", Author = herbert },
new Book { Title = "Emma", Year = 1815, Pages = 474, Genre = "Classic", Author = austen },
new Book { Title = "Persuasion", Year = 1817, Pages = 249, Genre = "Classic", Author = austen });
Dojo.Eq("books with 400+ pages", new List<string> { "Dune Herbert 1965", "Emma Austen 1815" }, dojoRows.Select(r => $"{r.Title} {r.Author} {r.Year}").ToList());
Dojo.Check("selects only the columns it needs", !LibraryDb.LastSql.Contains("\"Pages\", ") && !LibraryDb.LastSql.Contains("\"Genre\""), LibraryDb.LastSql);
public Author Author { get; set; } = null!;

protected override void OnConfiguring(DbContextOptionsBuilder options) => options.UseSqlite("Data Source=catalogue.db").LogTo((id, level) => id == RelationalEventId.CommandExecuted, e => { Commands++; LastSql = ((CommandExecutedEventData)e).Command.CommandText; });
